records.department: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances / responsible public authority
records.coverage: Public-service grievances routed to participating Central Ministries/Departments and State/UT authorities; appeal guidance here is for Central Ministries/Departments.
records.description: File a service-delivery grievance, track it by registration number and review the authority response. Use the portal feedback and eligible appeal route when dissatisfied with a Central Ministry or Department disposal.
steps: Check that the matter is within CPGRAMS scope, then register or sign in and choose the relevant authority.
Describe the service problem and previous application or complaint reference accurately; submit through the portal and save its registration number.
Use View Status and Reminder/Clarification to follow up.
After disposal, review the response and give feedback. Where the Central Ministry/Department appeal option is enabled, use it if dissatisfied.
conditions: CPGRAMS excludes RTI matters, court-related/subjudice matters and other categories listed on its official pages. Personal or family disputes are also outside the DARPG grievance scope.
State/UT grievances are forwarded to the concerned government; follow up with that government about pendency.

The CPGRAMS FAQ specifies 21 days for grievance redress, with an interim reply explaining delay. This is grievance-handling guidance, not a guaranteed completion time for the underlying certificate, licence or benefit.
The FAQ allows an appeal against a dissatisfied Central Ministry/Department disposal within 30 days; use the portal eligibility and feedback process.
Grievances emailed to CPGRAMS are not entertained. Use its grievance portal or published offline route.
records.fees: No government fee for filing a grievance on CPGRAMS. A Common Service Centre may charge for assisted filing.

records.department: Department of Personnel and Training / selected Central public authority
records.coverage: Indian citizens requesting information from Central Ministries/Departments and Central public authorities available on RTI Online.
records.description: Request existing official information or records, such as recorded action on an application, through the Central RTI portal. RTI seeks information; it does not itself approve a service application or resolve a grievance.
steps: Confirm that the information is held by a Central public authority listed on the portal.
Choose Submit Request and clearly identify the records or information sought.
Pay the prescribed application fee or upload the required BPL proof when claiming the exemption; save the registration number.
Track the reply through View Status. If the RTI response is missing after the applicable period or the decision is disputed, check the first-appeal procedure for that RTI request.
conditions: Do not use this portal for State Government public authorities, including Government of NCT Delhi; such requests are returned without refund. Use the relevant state route or Public Information Officer.
Section 7 normally requires an RTI decision within 30 days; life-or-liberty information has a 48-hour rule. Statutory exceptions, transfers and fee-payment intervals can affect the calculation.
A first appeal is normally filed within 30 days of the RTI decision or expiry of the applicable response period. Delayed appeals may be admitted for sufficient cause.
The first appellate authority normally decides within 30 days, extendable to a total of 45 days with written reasons.
These periods apply to the RTI process, not to the original government-service request. Information remains subject to the RTI Act exemptions.
records.fees: Central RTI application: INR 10 for a non-BPL applicant. BPL applicants are exempt with the required certificate. Additional information-copying charges may be notified. No fee for a first appeal on this portal.

records.coverage: Official RTI Act and guidance; links to Central and State information-commission and RTI resources.
records.description: Read the official RTI Act and find state RTI resources before choosing where to request records. For a state or local authority, confirm its Public Information Officer and the state-specific application route.
steps: Identify the public authority holding the records.
Use the official RTI guidance and state links to confirm the correct authority, application route and applicable rules.
conditions: This guidance page is not an RTI submission form.
The Central RTI Online portal is not the application route for State Government authorities or Government of NCT Delhi.
A service delay does not automatically trigger an RTI filing; choose a grievance route for redress and an RTI route when you need records.
